content: Baloxavir marboxil is indicated for the treatment of acute, uncomplicated influenza in patients aged 5 years and older who have been symptomatic for 48 hours or less. It is suitable for individuals who are otherwise healthy or at high risk of developing influenza-related complications. The absorption of baloxavir marboxil can be significantly reduced when co-administered with substances containing polyvalent cations, such as calcium, magnesium, aluminum, iron, and other metals. These cations can form chelates with baloxavir, leading to decreased gastrointestinal absorption and reduced plasma levels of the drug. This interaction has been demonstrated in animal studies, particularly in monkeys, where concurrent use with calcium, aluminum, or iron resulted in significantly lower plasma concentrations of baloxavir. However, human studies to confirm these findings have not been conducted. Specific substances that can interfere with baloxavir absorption include magnesium supplements, aluminum hydroxide, calcium carbonate, calcium acetate, calcium chloride, calcium citrate, calcium gluconate, iron supplements (e.g., ferrous fumarate, ferrous sulfate, ferric citrate, ferric carboxymaltose), multivitamins containing minerals, and other similar agents. These interactions necessitate avoiding or using alternative drugs to prevent reduced efficacy of baloxavir. Furthermore, the use of baloxavir marboxil may decrease the effectiveness of live attenuated influenza vaccines (LAIV) administered intranasally. This is due to potential pharmacodynamic antagonism, as antiviral agents like baloxavir may inhibit the replication of the live vaccine virus, thereby reducing vaccine efficacy. Close monitoring or modification of therapy is recommended when these agents are used concurrently. Lastly, immunosuppressive agents, such as ublituximab, may reduce the effectiveness of baloxavir marboxil by increasing the risk of infections. Caution and close monitoring are advised in such cases.
